p: Enfield gets overlooked by a lot of Londoners, which is daft, because it's stuffed with green space and has a quirky claim to fame or two. The world's first cash machine was installed at the Barclays branch in Enfield Town back in 1967, and there's a plaque to prove it. Point that out to the kids on the way past and watch them try to work out what life was like before cards.

If Forty Hall and the Lee Valley are already on your list, add a couple more. Myddelton House Gardens at Bulls Cross is a lovely, slightly wild garden that was the life's work of the plantsman E. A. Bowles, and it's a gentle spot for grown-ups who need a quiet half-hour after the chaos of the arena. Over on the western side of the borough, Trent Country Park has woodland trails, open fields and plenty of room for a kickabout.

Getting to Enfield without a car is easy enough too. Trains run out from Liverpool Street to Enfield Town, and Enfield Chase station is on the line from Moorgate, so you can turn a jump session into a car-free day out from central London.

A tip from the parent playbook: book the session that suits your youngest rather than your oldest. Teens will happily bounce anywhere, but a toddler in the wrong session can get overwhelmed fast. Pack a spare top for the journey home, and something to eat in the car, because jumping is hungry work and the grumbles start the minute the shoes go back on.
